name: realigning
note: The one setting that makes the design's central thesis work. A lean push scales by how decisively a race was won and never says what an UNCONTESTED win does. Reading a walkover as worth one pip takes the map from a driftless walk (mean |lean| 0.13, 0.2 states realigned a game) to a board that genuinely realigns (1.44, 7.4). Play this against `tuned` to see the difference the rule makes.

placeholders.resolution.tieBreak: The resolution rule says only 'higher total wins'. Even break is what makes edge 0 exactly 50%; a table needs a real rule.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.extremistPrimary: Extremism is a primary bonus and a general penalty, and no magnitude was ever printed.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.crossBenchPrimaryPenalty: Cross-benching is a primary penalty, and no magnitude was printed.
placeholders.lean.decayFrequency: Open question 1 -- SETTLED 2026-08-31 by arithmetic, not simulation. Annual decay is -2 per cycle against a maximum push of +2, so sustained blowouts net zero and lean pins at 2 forever: realignment is impossible. Biennial (-1) against margin-based pushes accumulates. See engine/rules/lean.test.ts and findings/decay-push-tradeoff.ts.
placeholders.lean.governorPushes: Open question; 'never' falls out of the priority rule, 'with-lean' is the alternative under test.
placeholders.lean.maxLean: No cap is stated. Without one, lean is unbounded.
placeholders.draft.districtsPerPack: Open: district-to-candidate ratio sets map fill rate and turn density.
placeholders.game.victory: Open question -- STILL OPEN, and now with evidence that none of the four original candidates works. Term-based conditions (two/three terms) terminate tightly but concentrate all value in one race: the SAME agent pool goes from 28% to 90% purely by switching points -> three-terms. Bills-passed keeps the field balanced (top 33%) but leaves 37-42% of games unfinished and runs to a median 34-49 years. Shipping points + a year cap as the least-bad playable default. See hf7y/american-cycle#13, still open.
placeholders.economy.*: The economy is described as a shape (random walk with memory, 2d6 roll-under on accumulated G) but prints no bounds or step sizes.
placeholders.legislature.reactionGoodOnRollAtLeast: A reaction is rolled immediately on passage, and nothing says on what.
placeholders.hand.bonus*: These were printed without saying per-seat or per-office. Read per seat they are a runaway: a player holding 20 Senate seats draws 32 cards a cycle. The original 'base 12 with president +2 is a 17% edge' is 2/12, which only parses as per-office. Implemented per office held.
placeholders.game.victory (ties): The victory condition was left open, and nothing was said about ties on final score, which are common. Placeholder is a coin flip. Resolving by lowest seat -- the natural coding accident -- manufactures a 25pp seat bias that does not exist.
placeholders.game.deckOutEnds: Deck-out was named as the ending, but also has defeated politicians circulate back through the draft. Circulation wins: talon+discard GROW from 79 to 273 cards over a hundred years, so deck-out is unreachable and cannot be the backstop it was treated as.
placeholders.lean.uncontestedPush: A push scales with how decisively a race was won, and nothing says what a walkover does -- a race nobody contested has no margin at all. This is the single highest-leverage undecided rule in the design: 0 leaves the map a driftless random walk and the central thesis unimplemented; 1 produces genuine realignment. See hf7y/american-cycle#10, still open, and hf7y/american-cycle#51.
placeholders.primaryGeneral.billCounterPips: A good reaction rewards yes-voters and a bad one penalises them at the next election, in both rounds, and that the card's accumulated counters are read off at resolution -- but prints no magnitude. One pip a counter is a stand-in.
placeholders.resolution.incumbencyPrimary: Incumbency was called "a calibration check on +1", but a primary is 1d6 vs 1d6 (SD 2.42) against a general's 3d6 (SD 4.18), so one scalar cannot serve both rounds. 4 puts contested primary incumbent survival at 91.2%. NOTE the benchmark population: the ~98% renomination rate quoted for real House incumbents is over ALL primaries including unopposed ones, so it is not the matching figure. Real CONTESTED survival is unverified.
placeholders.resolution.crossOfficeIncumbency: The stepping stone to higher office, flat. One number for every pair of offices: the primary/general asymmetry a table would encode is already emergent from the board, and the history refutes it (sitting House members won 61% of Senate primaries and 63% of the generals).
placeholders.primaryGeneral.crossBenchCap: The accumulated counters are simply read off, and uncapped they read ~30. But cross-benching is also structurally necessary to pass anything at a 60% Senate threshold, so an uncapped record makes cooperation career-ending. 3 puts the mean at 2.35 pips, 0.97 of the primary's 2.42 SD.
